feature.title: Coco Doctor
feature.brief: Add a read-only cocoframe doctor command that helps developers, CI, and AI clients quickly diagnose CocoFrame project, dependency, configuration, generated-artifact, security, build, and environment problems through actionable human output and a stable machine-readable JSON contract.

objective.value: Add a read-only cocoframe doctor command that helps developers, CI, and AI clients quickly diagnose CocoFrame project, dependency, configuration, generated-artifact, security, build, and environment problems through actionable human output and a stable machine-readable JSON contract.

value: Application developers running local diagnostics
CI pipelines evaluating project health
AI clients consuming machine-readable diagnostics

success-outcome.value: One command identifies actionable CocoFrame project problems with stable diagnostic codes, safe evidence, remediation guidance, documentation references, and consistent exit status without exposing secrets.

value: User runs cocoframe doctor in a project
Doctor resolves the project root and environment
Doctor runs safe read-only checks
Doctor aggregates and deterministically orders diagnostics
Doctor renders human output or a versioned JSON document
Doctor exits with a status derived from the result
Given a healthy project, when doctor runs, then it exits 0 with no error diagnostics
Given one or more error diagnostics, when doctor completes, then it exits 1
Given an internal doctor failure, then it exits 2 with a sanitized failure
Given --json, output is a versioned contract with no interleaved human logs
Default checks do not modify files, perform network requests, or reveal secrets
Every diagnostic includes code, severity, category, message, sanitized evidence, suggestion, and documentation reference
Expensive checks run only when --deep is explicitly selected
CLI, CI, and Agent Bridge consume the same diagnostic engine and contract
Terminal from the project root through cocoframe doctor
An explicit project through cocoframe doctor <path>
CI through cocoframe doctor --json
Agent Bridge through the read-only project.doctor tool
--json emits machine-readable output
--deep enables build and other expensive validation
--strict makes warnings produce exit status 1
Without --strict warning-only results exit 0
A healthy project emits a concise passed-check summary
A non-CocoFrame directory reports PROJECT_NOT_FOUND with recovery guidance
Configuration load failures identify the related file without exposing sensitive values
Missing or incompatible dependencies produce dependency diagnostics
Stale generated artifacts include the appropriate regeneration command
Unreadable files produce sanitized diagnostics without including sensitive content
A failed or timed-out deep check produces a check-specific diagnostic
An unexpected doctor failure exits 2 and --json still emits a valid sanitized JSON document

Reuse discoverRoutes, discoverIslands, discoverStyles, discoverGlobalStyles, discoverUiComponents, and discoverIcons
Reuse the canonical routePatternFromFile parser
Reuse generated capability discovery for OpenAPI, clients, API reference, context, assets, and deployment manifests

responsive.value: Human output uses no fixed-width tables, wraps long paths and suggestions safely, and remains vertically readable in narrow terminals; JSON output is independent of terminal dimensions.

value: Read-only project filesystem access
Local package.json and dependency metadata
Canonical CocoFrame discovery and inspection engine
Canonical build pipeline in a temporary workspace for --deep
In-process Agent Bridge consumption with AbortSignal cancellation
No external providers or network requests
File and parsing failures become targeted diagnostics
A deep-check failure or timeout does not prevent independent checks from completing
Cancellation stops work promptly and returns a sanitized status
Rely on local operating-system permissions; no application authentication is required
Resolve and confine the project root safely
Do not follow symlinks to read outside the workspace
Default checks do not execute project source or configuration
Deep build does not import or execute the application bundle
Render project files as relative paths
Never output environment values, cookies, tokens, authorization headers, passwords, private keys, or sensitive file contents
Bound the size and number of files read
Agent Bridge remains read-only and enforces cancellation and workspace confinement
Collect no automatic telemetry
JSON records mode and counts for checks, passed, warning, error, skipped, and internal failure
Every check has a stable ID and status
Diagnostics are deterministically ordered
CI uses exit status and JSON as evidence
No event is transmitted or persisted outside the process
Default output omits timing so snapshots remain stable; doctor performance is measured by separate tests or benchmarks
Unexpected failures expose a stable sanitized code suitable for user reports
Default doctor completes within 2 seconds on the reference project without running a build
--deep has a default timeout of 60 seconds
Cancellation is checked between every check and major filesystem operation
At most 10000 files are inspected per run
Source files are limited to 1 MiB per file
At most 1000 diagnostics are returned and the result sets truncated true when the limit is reached
Filesystem operations use bounded concurrency
JSON output never embeds full source files or other large payloads
No browser-performance limit applies because the feature is CLI-only
Release as an additive command without migration or feature flag
Release the doctor engine, CLI command, and Agent Bridge project.doctor tool in one coordinated package release
Start the JSON contract at version 1
Additive fields remain backward compatible; breaking changes increment the contract version
Never repurpose or silently change the meaning of a stable diagnostic code
The Agent Bridge tool is additive and read-only
Upgrading does not change project source or generated artifacts
Rollback uses the previous coordinated package release
Every release includes documentation, changelog, focused tests, and package smoke verification
